about: Names left out of electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), state by state, by the reason given. Figures are the Election Commission's and state Chief Electoral Officers', as reported in the sources cited; ECI's own press notes could not be fetched by this site's scripts (eci.gov.in refuses automated requests), so each figure links to the publication it was read from. A name 'left out of the draft' is not the same as a name finally deleted: the draft is followed by claims, objections and hearings, and the final roll can be larger. Figures written in lakh or crore by the source are stored rounded and marked approximate.

reasons.label: Enrolled in more than one place
Form not returned, refused, or no reason given

phases.label: Phase I
phases.note: Announced 24 June 2025; draft roll 1 August, final roll 30 September 2025.

phases.label: Phase II
phases.coverage: Nine states and three union territories
phases.note: Enumeration from 27 October 2025; drafts published 16–31 December 2025; final rolls February 2026. Across the 12, about 6.56 crore names were left out of the drafts: 4.64 crore shifted, 1.46 crore dead, 44.06 lakh multiple registrations.

phases.label: Phase III
phases.coverage: Sixteen states and three union territories
phases.note: Ordered 14 May 2026, covering about 36.73 crore electors; drafts published from August 2026, final rolls due from November. Reason breakdowns are published so far only as name lists on state CEO websites, not as counts.

draft.note: ECI: 22.34 lakh dead; 36.28 lakh permanently shifted or not traceable by BLOs; 7.01 lakh registered in two places. Deccan Herald rounds the shifted figure to about 35 lakh.

final.note: 21.53 lakh added through Form 6 and 3.66 lakh more removed after the draft; the 9,968 'other' had no reason recorded, per the Bihar CEO's records reported by ADR. The Supreme Court asked ECI on 7 October 2025 to explain the post-draft deletions.

draft.note: 18.7% of the earlier roll; 'shifted' is reported as permanent migration.

The four reasons sum to 57,63,294, about 58,000 short of the difference between the rolls; reports describe the duplicates as 'duplicate or fictitious entries'. A further 1.67 crore electors were put under scrutiny; scrutiny is not deletion.

final.note: By April 2026 the revision had removed about 91 lakh names in all: some 63 lakh from the draft and claims stage and about 27 lakh more declared ineligible after judicial adjudication. The 58 lakh draft figure and the 91 lakh total measure different stages.

draft.note: Duplicates are 3,39,278 per The Federal; Deccan Herald gives 3.98 lakh. 'Shifted' covers names found to have permanently shifted or migrated. Chennai alone accounted for 14,25,018.
'Shifted or absent' is names that had shifted or were not found at the registered address.
A further 8.40 lakh names were reported as not yet mapped to the earlier roll; unmapped is not deleted.
'Other' is forms not returned or refused. The five reasons sum to 24,08,513, ten more than the stated total. 8.65% of the roll.
Category figures are reported in lakh and so are approximate. About 11 lakh more electors were to be issued notices seeking documents; a notice is not a deletion.
Left-out total is the sum of the three reported categories.
20.6% of the roll, the highest share of any state or UT in Phase II. No breakdown by reason was found.

final.note: Net change of 206 names between the earlier and final rolls. No draft-stage breakdown was found.

draft.note: The CEO calls these 'uncollectable enumeration forms': 21.15% of the roll, excluded from the draft but not yet deleted. No count by reason has been published; claims run to 12 October and the final roll is due 16 November 2026.

More than 47 lakh excluded from the draft, with notices to over 33 lakh over record discrepancies; the CEO says a notice is not a deletion. The list of absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors is on the CEO Delhi website as names, not counts. Final roll due 4 November 2026.
Draft roll down about 1.5 lakh; no breakdown by reason found.
